messages:
Amanda: Quick heads-up — prepping the QBR for Activation this Friday. Major focus: sudden token burn spike and updated 60-day forecast. Need owners for a couple items.
Kenji: On it. Can you drop the latest forecast? I want to validate our assumptions around embed-heavy flows.
Amanda: Uploading now — see link to the sheet `QBR_activation_forecast_v3.xlsx` (drive). Highlights: +42% embed token usage month-over-month, two big jobs from new customer segments.
Raj: Noted. Two questions: 1) Do we have a knob to throttle embeddings on Dedicated vs Hosted for this account? 2) Any credits/commit changes on the contract we should surface at renewal?
Emily: For (1) we can route heavy batches to Dedicated if they have reserved capacity — otherwise suggest prefix caching + smaller batch_size. For (2) the account is still on monthly usage; no commit. Renewal risk flag if we don't propose a cost cap.
Amanda: Good call. Action items: Kenji to run a quick cost simulation with prefix caching on/off; Raj to draft renewal talking points with a proposed commit tier; Emily to prepare spend alert thresholds we can suggest.
Kenji: Will run sims today. Quick note on sims — need representative prompt mix. Amanda, can you paste a 5-min sample log?
Amanda: Pasting snippet from logs (sanitized):
```
user_id,endpoint,tokens
acct_987,embed,1200
acct_987,chat,340
acct_987,embed,980
```
That should be representative of peak-hour activity.
OnboardBot: Reminder set — "QBR prep sync" scheduled Thu 10:30am PT. Attendees: Amanda, Kenji, Raj, Emily.
Raj: For renewal deck I'll sketch 2 options: (A) conservative commit with buffer + batching guidance, (B) flexible monthly + dynamic routing + spend alerts. Will call out expected unit cost delta (~25% vs commit).
Emily: For spend alerts: suggest thresholds at 50%, 75%, 90% of month-to-date forecast and a hard cap webhook to cut non-critical embeddings. I can prototype the webhook text.
Kenji: Simulation results: with prefix caching + batch_size=8 we save ~28% on embed token cost in peak window. Without caching it's only ~7%. I'll add a simple graph to the sheet.
Amanda: Perfect. Two remaining asks before Thu: Raj — first draft of renewal slides; Emily — sample alert messages; Kenji — add sims to sheet. Ping me once done.
Raj: Got it, will share draft by EOD tomorrow.
Emily: I'll post sample webhook payloads and a short playbook for on-call in the sheet today.
Amanda: Thanks team. Also capture any customer feedback about latency vs cost trade-offs in the deck — they mentioned quality > latency in last sync. Raj, note that for negotiation.
Raj: Noted — will surface that as preference for smaller quantization changes and emphasis on routing instead of aggressive quantization.
Amanda: Closing loop — if anything changes I’ll update the thread. :thumbsup:
